issues.note: Intransitive self-shutoff use sits under a causative definition with only transitive patterns.
Turn someone off something is typical; patterns are a closed list and collocations hold this.
Sense 1 already names a supply of water or gas; the use is covered.
A supply that stops working is awkward; the switch-or-control objection is overstated.
The self-shutoff intransitive use needs a subsense or its own definition.
The oven example means stop working and does not fit make something stop.
Example misfits the causative definition.
Close the light is a genuine, frequent learner error, and the correction is right.
Names a specific open/close trap, not a generic translation warning.
The stress contrast with the noun is stated in both the pronunciation notes and the adaptation note.
The core idea is a sentence, as house style requires; the objection is taste.
The bored or put-off sense is informal, not formal.
The incorrect and correct forms are reversed; turn off it is wrong.
Off the main road is preposition plus object; the patterns are correct.
The sense covers both effects; the objection is taste.
Disable is not a true synonym for turning off lights or water.
The formal label contradicts the informal use shown in the examples.
Switch on is an antonym listed among the synonyms.
The intransitive claim rests on an example that misfits the causative definition.
The pronoun-position forms are reversed.
The common intransitive self-shutoff use lacks a fitting definition or subsense.

findings.F1: Sense 1 defines a causative transitive use, but the intransitive self-shutoff example (oven turns off by itself) has no fitting definition or subsense.
findings.F2: The stress contrast between turn off and turnoff is stated in both pronunciation.notes and the pronunciation adaptation note.
findings.F3: Sense 3 (make someone bored or dislike something) is labeled formal; it is informal.
findings.F4: The learner error on pronoun position has its incorrect and correct forms swapped.
findings.F5: disable-v is listed as a synonym of sense 1 but is not a true synonym.
findings.F6: switch-on-phrv, an antonym, is listed among the synonyms of sense 1.
